It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Kamo Shrine'''|加茂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

It is the general tutelary shrine of the Irino area, standing inside {{ill|Irino Pine Grove|ja|入野松原|qid=Q131912175}}, a nationally designated {{ill|Place of Scenic Beauty|ja|名勝|ro|Loc pitoresc (Japonia)|zh_yue|名勝|qid=Q11414752}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The enshrined deities are as follows{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.
* Principal deity: {{ill|Kamo-wake-ikazuchi-no-Kami|Q11634943|qid=Q11634943|lt=Wakeikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}
* Co-enshrined deity: {{ill|Hachiman|ar|هاتشيمان|az|Haçiman|ca|Hachiman|de|Hachiman|el|Χατσίμαν|es|Hachiman|eu|Hachiman|fa|هاچیمان|fi|Hachiman|fr|Hachiman|hu|Hacsiman|id|Hachiman|it|Hachiman|ja|八幡神|ko|하치만 신|mni|ꯍꯆꯤꯃꯥꯟ|my|ဟချိမန်း|pl|Hachiman|pt|Hachiman|ru|Хатиман|simple|Hachiman|sl|Hačiman|sv|Hachiman|tok|jan sewi Kasiman|tr|Hachiman|uk|Хачіман|uz|Hachiman|vi|Hachiman|wuu|八幡神|zh|八幡神|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman-gū}}
Alternative theories include: {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|Q506610|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami}} in ''Shingi Shiryo''{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}; unknown deity in ''{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}''{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}; {{ill|Okamotsumi|ja|大鴨積命|qid=Q106412720}} in ''Tosa no Kuni Shikisha-kō''{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}; and Ōkamozumi-no-Mikoto in ''Henkaimatsufu''{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

== History ==
Foundation is unknown. In the {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is identified with the "Kamo Shrine" listed in {{ill|Hata District, Kōchi|ceb|Hata-gun|es|Distrito de Hata|fr|District de Hata|id|Distrik Hata, Kōchi|it|Distretto di Hata|ja|幡多郡|ko|하타군|pl|Powiat Hata|uk|Повіт Хата|uz|Hata tumani|zh|幡多郡|qid=Q1132241}}, {{ill|Tosa Province|ar|دوشو|cs|Tosa (provincie)|de|Provinz Tosa|es|Provincia de Tosa|fa|ولایت توسا|fi|Tosan provinssi|fr|Province de Tosa|gl|Provincia de Tosa|id|Provinsi Tosa|it|Tosa (provincia)|ja|土佐国|ko|도사국|lt|Tosos žemė|nl|Tosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Tosa|ru|Тоса (провинция)|sh|Tosa (provincija)|simple|Tosa Province|sk|Tosa (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тоса|th|แคว้นโทซะ|tr|Tosa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тоса|zh|土佐國|zh_min_nan|Tosa-kok|qid=Q857330}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

According to tradition, Kamo Shrine originally stood at Kamo-yashiki in Irino Honmura, while Hachimangū stood at Hachiman-hara in Hayasaki; the two shrines later became one and moved into Irino Pine Grove{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. ''Tosa no Kuni Shikisha-kō'' also says both shrines were originally in Honmura, though the date of unification is unknown{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. ''Nishiura Kaiken Nikki'' likewise says both were in Honmura{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

Also, the "Irino Ōgata no Gō Chikenchō" of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} 17 ({{ill|1589|ab|1589|af|1589|als|1589|am|1589 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1589|ar|1589|ary|1589|arz|1589|ast|1589|avk|1589|az|1589|azb|۱۵۸۹ (میلادی)|bar|1589|bcl|1589|be|1589|be_x_old|1589|bg|1589|bn|১৫৮৯|bpy|মারি ১৫৮৯|br|1589|bs|1589.|ca|1589|cdo|1589 nièng|ceb|1589|ckb|١٥٨٩|crh|1589|cs|1589|cv|1589|cy|1589|da|1589|de|1589|diq|1589|el|1589|eml|1589|eo|1589|es|1589|et|1589|eu|1589|fa|۱۵۸۹ (میلادی)|fi|1589|fo|1589|fr|1589|frr|1589|fur|1589|fy|1589|ga|1589|gan|1589年|gcr|1589|gd|1589|gl|1589|he|1589|hi|१५८९|hr|1589.|ht|1589 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1589|hy|1589|hyw|1589 թուական|ia|1589|id|1589|ilo|1589|io|1589|is|1589|it|1589|ja|1589年|jv|1589|ka|1589|kaa|1589|kk|1589 жыл|ko|1589년|krc|1589 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1589|la|1589|lb|1589|lij|1589|lmo|1589|lt|1589 m.|lv|1589. gads|mai|१५८९|map_bms|1589|mdf|1589|mg|1589|mhr|1589|mi|1589|mk|1589|mr|इ.स. १५८९|mrj|1589 и|ms|1589|my|၁၅၈၉|mzn|۱۵۸۹|nah|1589|nap|1589|nds|1589|new|सन् १५८९|nl|1589|nn|1589|no|1589|nrm|1589|nso|1589|oc|1589|or|୧୫୮୯|os|1589-æм аз|pa|1589|pl|1589|pnb|1589|pt|1589|qu|1589|ro|1589|ru|1589 год|rue|1589|sa|१५८९|sah|1589|scn|1589|sd|1589ع|se|1589|sh|1589.|shn|1589|simple|1589|sk|1589|sl|1589|smn|1589|sq|1589|sr|1589|su|1589|sv|1589|sw|1589|ta|1589|tg|Соли 1589|th|พ.ศ. 2132|tk|1589|tl|1589|tly|1589|tr|1589|tt|1589 ел|uk|1589|ur|1589ء|uz|1589|vec|1589|vi|1589|vls|1589|wa|1589|war|1589|wuu|1589年|xmf|1589|yi|1589|zh|1589年|zh_classical|一五八九年|zh_min_nan|1589 nî|zh_yue|1589年|qid=Q6759}}) records shrine lands of 5 villages and 3 chō 6 tan in Irino Ōgata-gō{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, during the {{ill|1707 Hōei earthquake|Q2001581|qid=Q2001581|lt=great Hōei earthquake}} of {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} 4 ({{ill|1707|Q6841|qid=Q6841}}), the shrine buildings suffered tsunami damage{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. According to ''Nanroshi'', the shrine buildings floated in floodwater but returned to their original place when the tsunami receded{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. A monument recording this tsunami damage remains in the precincts{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. In earlier times, Rinzai temple Ōgata-zan Chōsen-ji served as the shrine's {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}} temple{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in the modern shrine ranking system{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}{{Sfn|Kamo Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.
